chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
"When two men lead one another in prayer, one of them leads the other, and he stands to his right; and if there are more than that, they stand behind him."
ai.seo_question: How should two or three people arrange themselves in prayer when one leads the other?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi’s Tahdhib, this hadith clarifies the specific spatial arrangement for small congregations, distinguishing the etiquette of standing to the right for a single companion versus the standard row formation for larger groups. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on order (nazm) and the hierarchical respect shown to the Imam during prayer, ensuring the validity of the congregational act even in minimal numbers.
